digest.component_or_area: Jira write dispatch and retry orchestration
propositions: Jira writes across Cloud ACLI/REST and DC SDK routes can multiply or leave acceptance ambiguous under timeout; a provider-neutral operation/outcome contract with stable logical id, postcondition, invocation/request counts, and disposition must unify both providers.
Each selected operation is limited to three physical invocations and 15 seconds cumulative sleep with exponential backoff [2s,3s), then [4s,5s), where provider Retry-After is a lower bound.

Cloud summary-only writes use one ACLI process per write with primary-store REST recovery (no ACLI JQL) and one-attempt/no-sleep policy, while DC uses a dedicated executor client with max_retries=0 and GET/PUT/GET invocation pattern.

Desired summary observed after timeout means recovered success; ambiguous or failed observation returns non-replaying commit_unknown; authoritative delay over budget returns retry_not_before without sleep.

Every terminal outcome records exactly one redacted per-mutation message capped at 512 Unicode code points, with completion logs containing logical id, disposition, invocation/request counts, cleanup status, retry_not_before, and one redacted message (whole log capped at 1,024 code points).

Constructor-injected internal route selector defaults to legacy in S1 (tests explicit), adds no config/env surface, and S3 owns venue-gated validation and default-on cutover with durable deferral and bridge retirement.
